chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Can a man pray while he is veiled (covering his head and body with a single garment)?' He said, 'As for praying on the ground, no; and as for praying on the animal (mount), there is no problem.'

key_terms.مُتَلَثِّمٌ: One who covers himself with a single garment (veiled/hooded)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray while wearing a single garment that covers the head and body?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the fiqh of *salat al-mutalaththim* (prayer while wrapped in a single garment), distinguishing between the ground and riding animals. While praying on the ground in this state is generally considered makruh or impermissible due to the lack of proper posture and dignity, it is permissible on a mount where the physical constraints of riding make full prostration difficult. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing ritual purity with practical ease (*rukhas*) in varying circumstances.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzaan, from Hammad Bin Isa from Rabie, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws, said,
‘I said to himasws, ‘Can the man pray Salāt while he is veiled?’ So heasws said: ‘As for upon the ground, so no, and as for upon the animal, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Rib‘i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a man’s performing Salah (prayer) with his face veiled. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not permissible while on the ground; however, while riding on a stumper is not an offense.’”
